The repaired review-fixes/faults-26.1-R8.json passes 2/7 A261-058 inputs; five still lack actionable next steps. A261-059 passes 2/6 diagnostic cases. Missing-item/static-ID and cosmetic indentation are accepted without errors. A structurally valid SQL report baseline compiles, and the SQL-only malformed variant is also accepted; the original fixture's region errors did not establish SQL diagnostic precision. Catalog proposals and semantic-capability gaps require review; runtime semantics and expectations are unchanged.

APEX 26.2 offline profile/MMD identity and two starters containing all six recipes compile; CodeScan advisories remain separate. Original extension-26.2-final.json failed A262-001 with VALIDATION_FAILED / exit 1, but changing the profile of 26.2 sources tested compiler refusal before proving the target. The corrected review-fixes/extension-26.2-R8.json records the target check as not_run: its connection prerequisite returns ORACLE_COMMAND_FAILED / exit 1 and a valid 26.1 source/lock is still required. A262-003 remains 17/21 top-three golden hits (80.95%), below 90%; the repeated warm median is 0.71 ms. Four exact misses/top-three lists and proposed release-exclusivity wording are in review-fixes/R8-triage.md. No connected 26.2 parity or local-versus-remote comparison is qualified.

The Claude usage adapter is implemented and verified against a historical transcript: an independent hand sum agrees at 102,416 normalized total tokens (claude-usage-real.json). Its scripted two-turn check remains pending. R2 reanalysis of both prior native reports found no write-classification changes; original sessions were preserved. Both hosts reran AGT-001/004/007/008/011 three times: agent-codex-26.1-final.json passes 11/15, and agent-claude-26.1-final.json passes 6/15, with zero observed import/browser/secret violations. Two correct Ukrainian FK-absence answers were initially rejected by the English-only oracle; reanalysis corrected them without rerunning models. Claude instruction reads are observed in all 15 sessions; its local Edit and dictionary attempts include native permission-denial hints. AGT-007 still fails citation checks, with three manual semantic-review entries per host. Original raw measurements are preserved in review-fixes/R6-before-fk-reanalysis-.json, with triage in review-fixes/hand-back.md. AGT-007 independent semantic review is needs_review, while missing plugin use/citation still fails automatic checks. Native model/effort defaults are not pinned, active Codex payload binding remains unproven and timings are descriptive. The review repository checks passed typecheck/lint, 413 unit tests with one optional skip and 107 contracts; build/bundle/documentation/site checks are recorded in the hand-back.

The reusable APEX 26.1 server qualification catalog defines 67 A261- baseline and quality/performance scenarios covering every current acceptance ID, with authorization boundaries, functional expectations and performance/token evidence requirements. APEX 26.2 has a separate extension catalog and separate reports; agent, Codex/Claude host and Bitcoin catalogs are also present. The current-build stdio MCP harness exercised live identity, metadata, references, working-copy baseline, Oracle validation and read-only planning on an authorized remote APEX 26.1.5 test application. Three explicitly authorized title-only full imports across MCP restarts and a fresh ship returning the original title succeeded. An independent final full export matched all 21 initial files, including hidden Oracle metadata, byte for byte. This verifies application-source preservation; it does not qualify the separate backup-restore command, business DML, browser behavior or native-host lifecycle. SQLcl 26.3 compiled the actual 26.1 sources; no 26.2 application result is claimed.

The run found and repaired two defects: hyphenated APEX workspace names were incorrectly rejected as SQL identifiers, and MCP apply forwarded an explicitly saved plan into plan mode, causing pre-write INVALID_INPUT. Regression checks retain strict SQL schema identifiers and route the exact saved plan to the existing apply worker, which still validates expiry, source/target drift, production policy, backup, coordination and grant handling before writes. Current local checks passed typecheck/lint, 396 unit cases with one optional case skipped, 70 contracts and 46 installer cases. The packaging matrix passed 28 cases initially and its remaining npm inventory case passed after moving the temporary npm cache into writable private storage; the original sandbox failure is retained. Test latency reports are descriptive smoke samples, not qualified p95 or an SLA. Oracle CodeScan reported seven existing advisory security findings, separately from compiler success.

Private evidence is under ignored docs/evidence/plugin-server/. Actual Codex token checkpoints read cumulative host usage only, retain cache accounting and mark missing/stale/reset/cross-session data unavailable; no CLI/MCP token estimates are reported as billing. Initial harness failures and sandbox listener/staging/cache limitations are preserved separately from repaired results. See the reusable [test procedure](../tests/plugin-server/README.md) for reproducible execution and evidence boundaries.

The requested APEX 26.1 browser follow-up passed nine host-browser checks on the existing test application: authorized login, authenticated reload, navigation disclosure, keyboard control, narrow shell, logout, protected Home, empty-login rejection and subsequent valid login. The embedded panel's effective narrow width was 325 pixels after requesting 390; the report records both dimensions. This is application-shell/session evidence, not business CRUD or Composer runtime qualification. Nine reusable browser definitions accompany the 67-case baseline/quality catalog. The active native MCP rejected the hyphenated workspace while the current-build CLI URL handoff succeeded; an updated bundle and fresh native session remain necessary before claiming installed-host parity.

The read-only performance follow-up passed 20 repetitions for each of six scenarios, with one excluded warm-up per scenario: fresh MCP startup/reference, warm reference search, warm project summary, live three-kind metadata batch, Oracle compiler validation and full-import planning. All 120 measured samples and six warm-ups passed; the run took 390.06 seconds and made 128 MCP tool calls. Median/nearest-rank p95 was 9.62/12.79 seconds for metadata and 6.86/7.96 seconds for planning. Warm offline compiler validation used the persistent SQLcl JVM (0.228/0.288 seconds), while connected work opened fresh vendor sessions. Oracle CodeScan retained seven existing advisory findings. This is a current-build, same-run distribution with concurrent browser observations and whole-host token deltas; no controlled historical regression baseline, per-call model billing, repeated import throughput or installed-host performance claim is established.

Per-operation SQLcl instrumentation records process readiness/spawn, saved-connection connect, execution and total durations, transport, reuse, mutation and bounded caller labels. CLI connect time remains unavailable because it belongs to the script execution interval. Recorders isolate concurrent operations and contain no SQL, bindings or usernames. Ship result details and deployment journal transitions retain timings; journal timingPhase identifies the preceding phase whose work was observed. Metadata responses add only session count/total SQLcl time by default; debugTimings: true includes the individual records. Scoped metadata reads now batch identity and all requested queries into one connected session, rejecting all rows on identity mismatch. Working-copy fingerprints batch identity and update metadata in one session. A full working-copy apply with the same read/deploy connection and no fresh export uses four connected sessions in fake-runner checks: start observation, post-freeze pre-import observation, import, post-import observation. Different connections keep a separate deploy identity check. Fresh-export paths reuse the start export as backup and retain the stronger post-freeze pre-import drift check (three total exports including plan); other export-backed paths retain the post-backup drift check; database scripts keep a post-freeze first-write barrier and exact local migration-history validation. Post-import metadata supplies the successful checkpoint. Cancellation, frozen-source checks and interrupted-write ownership remain intact. The optional same-session import guard is deferred because MCP R4 lacks a proven error-stop contract. The APEX 26.1.5 read-only follow-up passed 40 measured samples and two excluded warm-ups (20 per scenario), with 44 MCP calls in 188.97 seconds. Metadata median/p95 changed from 9.62/12.79 to 5.42/6.03 seconds; full-import plan changed from 6.86/7.96 to 3.13/4.04 seconds. Each used one fresh connected session; steady-state planning also used one reused offline compiler session. Median summed spawn/connect/execute intervals were 0.70 ms/null/5411.46 ms for metadata and 0.46 ms/null/3138.48 ms for plan. CLI spawn measures OS process creation; JVM startup and connection setup remain inside execute. Parallel plan intervals can overlap. These are separate runs on the same recorded machine/target, without controlled network/load/cache conditions. Whole-host token checkpoints are retained separately from per-call billing, which remains unavailable. The four-session apply reduction is estimated at about 12.45 seconds of saved session time using the 3.11-second read-only observation median as a proxy; it is estimated, not measured on Oracle. No import, database write or DDL was run in this follow-up. Typecheck, lint, 408 unit checks (one optional check skipped), 70 contracts, build, documentation and bundle checks passed.

Run the relevant checks in [testing](testing.md) against the current source. Local unit, contract, installer, documentation and packaging checks establish their stated fixture/build behavior. Oracle compilation, connected imports, authenticated application browsing and fresh native model-host execution require separate checks on an authorized target. Browser checks are not inferred from compiler/import success.

The current parity source passed typecheck and lint, 383 unit checks (one additional check skipped), 62 contracts, 46 installer checks and all 29 packaging cases. Claude Code 2.1.291 accepted the plugin and marketplace manifests with strict validation. The final unit run followed the completed build and had local-listener access for its ORDS protocol fixture; npm inventory used a private temporary cache. These are repository, manifest and subprocess checks, not native model-host execution.

Host parity changes preserve the existing scoped deployment core. Both manifest launch adapters are checked from a relocated package, with equal tool contracts/reference results and shared managed connection state. Installer checks cover dual-host launch bindings, source-safe reinstall, Node changes and Claude metadata integrity. Source-bound validation and packaging results are recorded separately under ignored docs/evidence/host-parity/. Native Codex/Claude model-host execution and new Oracle/browser runs are not established by these subprocess/fixture checks. Managed setup still registers Codex only; Claude uses its native plugin commands.

On the explicitly authorized local Oracle APEX 26.2 target, page creation and isolated replacement passed Oracle compiler/import/readback checks. APEXlang restoration of the previous selected page also passed without a SQL application dump. A stopped verification was reconciled as already applied without replay; Oracle filenames are matched by unique page ID rather than alias spelling. New and changed shared LOV files passed isolated imports: their plans explicitly disclose full APEXlang observation, while backup, import and comparison retain the selected scope. A final separate full audit checks unrelated files and business-row counts; it is outside the page-only edit cycle.

The authenticated in-app browser showed the new dashboard's version marker, three zero-valued CRM cards, empty customer chart, demonstration chart and the changed shared LOV label. These observations establish this dashboard and dependency rendering, not full CRM CRUD or security qualification. Page replacement measured about 34 seconds including planning/apply/readback; new dashboard creation about 44 seconds. Shared-component creation/replacement measured about 42/49 seconds because native selected export is unavailable for these families. Local no-op measured about 30 milliseconds with zero Oracle calls. The earlier whole-export flow took about 48 seconds for plan/apply; these are individual local samples, not a controlled performance guarantee. Independent machines/homes still require external serialization.

The user reported successful live Claude Code verification on 2026-10-07. That session reported an isolated analytics-page import with --import-mode files on the local 26.2 target: an occupied page 40 blocked planning, page 70 imported, and ship mode:recover recognized the already-applied result after key-ordered classic report columns caused a readback mismatch. It also reported four expected regions and unchanged pages 40/50/60, with no browser check requested. These are session-reported observations; the follow-up commit review did not independently repeat Oracle or native-host execution.

On 2026-10-15 three working-copy sync defects found during recipe imports were fixed. Native selected export now issues one -expComponents call per component, because APEX 26.2 rejects a component list with ORA-20987 even for existing pages (reproduced with pages 1 and 10). The selected-source equivalence policy now reads scalar lists, binds fenced code to its property, ignores the order of uniquely named properties and groups and of key-ordered page, process-parameter and dynamic-action children with explicit sequences, and accepts single-line JSON-quoted code, upper-cased invoke identifiers and the defaults observed in native exports (invokeApi direction/dataType/ignoreOutput, items-event change, page cursorFocus and formAutoComplete, classic-report pagination). Planning treats server files that differ from the checkpoint only by these canonical forms as unchanged, including in the reviewed before side revalidated by apply, so a full import no longer blocks the next full or selected plan and no export is added after imports. On the local APEX 26.2 target, a two-new-page selected import, a selected import of an authored page with template-option lists and a selected import after a full import all succeeded with equivalent readback, and mode:recover closed a run interrupted before the fix; tests: 421 unit (one skip), 114 contract, 29 packaging. The equivalence policy now accepts key-ordered columns only for classic reports with unique explicit sequences; other region types, absent/duplicate sequences and changed column identities/query IDs remain strict. Conflict diagnostics name the overlapping files. Follow-up repository checks passed typecheck, lint, 32 focused equivalence/partial-import/partial-export tests and the checked-in plugin CLI/stdio MCP smoke. The source bundle and documentation were regenerated and checked. Full unit, contract, installer and packaging suites were not rerun for this follow-up.

The official inventory maintenance change passed complete archive/document/type/property reconciliation and 2,269 packaged MCP reads for all 389 definitions. Its focused checks cover exact pagination, ordinary component/property discovery, independently bound search bytes, recovery of incomplete/corrupt accelerators, integrity failure, release isolation, public Oracle enums and continued operation/diagnostic secret redaction. Independent temporary-copy forward checks also passed source refresh and synthetic MMD/new-release review decisions. These are library/compiler checks, not connected or native-host qualification.

Parity implementation checks did not register the bundle into the user's existing Codex or Claude Code profiles. Local contracts exercise relocated MCP subprocesses, and Claude's native CLI validates manifests without starting a model session. The user's subsequent Claude Code verification is reported above; independent fresh cache/skill reload and model-driven tool qualification remain open for both hosts. Parity implementation and follow-up review used isolated fixtures without changing global connection, credential, toolchain or deployment-history state.

Release readiness requires source-bound reports for every mandatory gate. Generated reports are private working output under ignored docs/evidence/; their absence blocks readiness. No connected or native-host result is inferred from a local build.

The 2.3.0 repository integration checks passed on Node 24.21.0: 431 unit checks with one optional SQLcl pooling case skipped, 115 contracts, 46 installer checks and 29 packaging cases, plus lint, typecheck, documentation/site and bundle-integrity checks. Installer loopback fixtures passed with local-listener access. The final unit run used a private managed home and a completed build; earlier restricted-environment and concurrent-rebuild failures remain in private logs. Unsigned local packaging produced version 2.3.0 artifacts without publication; full readiness remains false. These local results do not qualify fresh native-host execution, connected Oracle, browser behavior or registry distribution. Private records are under docs/evidence/decisions/version-2.3.0/.

The offline Composer harness keeps its managed home outside the new project directory, preserving the initialization conflict guard. Composer now has an explicit 26.2 profile with six immutable @1.1.0 block packages and separate CRM/Service Desk blueprints. Real SQLcl build 26.3.0.260.1620 and vendor MMD 26.2.0+3479 compiled both complete scaffolds successfully; CRM materialization and repeat no-op checks passed. The adapters use exact lowercase report type enums and stable numeric process/saved-report mappings. Compiler/MMD mismatch checks remain mandatory. Fresh functional compiler records bind each new block to its generator, configuration and complete scaffold digest. Original 26.1 packages and records retain their true scope; old records cannot qualify the current generator or 26.2. This proof performs no database SQL, import, DML, authenticated browser or native model-host operation.

The retained publisher local-evidence exception is bound to 2.2.0 and does not apply to the current 2.3.0 source. Under the existing configuration, all nine source-bound qualification reports remain required for current-version npm and full readiness. Missing, failed and stale evidence blocks its applicable gate. Publication authorization, CI, package integrity, ownership and registry clean-install checks remain separate requirements; the GitHub release workflow remains disabled.

Host-parity teardown now awaits all MCP clients before removing their working directory, tracks clients before connection and retains close failures. Its focused macOS regression and all 62 contracts passed; the subsequent hosted CI passed Windows, macOS and both Linux matrix jobs. No CI workflow or database deployment safeguard was removed.

Actual isolated Codex registration/adoption/cache checks passed with the then-current package. A native conversation completed CLI Composer materialization and no-op; its MCP selected an older duplicate plugin because quoted dotted CLI overrides were interpreted as literal keys. A supported temporary config profile resolved that routing issue and actual MCP calls read the current 1.1.0 CRM blueprint and CRUD block. This was a configuration mismatch, not a current catalog defect. The user then stopped full external qualification. The already-started local import created only disposable app 92630 and the dedicated CMP fixture tables/API in APEXREST_262_TEST, with confirmed server verification and grant removal; runtime CRUD/browser qualification is incomplete. These narrower results do not establish all six external gates. Private records remain under ignored docs/evidence/.

 Repository automation

CI runs automatically only on pushes to main. Release and Oracle integration workflows are disabled in GitHub and gated off in their checked-in jobs. The publisher opts into the authorized npm target, subject to all required current evidence. Build, site generation and release dry-run create local output only.

Open checks are listed in [next actions](next-actions.md). Publication, tagging and database changes require their own applicable authorization.

 Documentation website

The Markdown pipeline generates tracked GitHub Pages output under docs/, with /apexrest/ routes, responsive grouped navigation, search, section links and previous flat .html guide URLs. site:check verifies generated freshness. The safety source is integrated before generation; The local browser verified current safety rules and the coverage route, navigation/search/anchors and a 390-pixel layout with contained table scrolling. The final generated site and packaging checks passed separately from these browser observations. This local work does not publish or verify revised live Pages output.

title: Next actions
text:
Next actions and verification limits

 Current review defects

- Fix the P1 remote SQL risk gap for parameterless function calls and calls within CTAS. Reproduce the exact remote planner/confirmation path; the 2026-10-31 review reconfirmed the existing defect without executing SQL on Oracle (SAFETY-01, A22).
- Fix the P1 exit-drain outcome classification: killing a live descendant after normal launcher exit must leave an interrupted/unknown write outcome, and a migration must not be marked succeeded without its completion marker (A14, A16). Cancel the separate drain timer after normal close so it cannot signal a reused process-group ID. Local shell and fake-Oracle workflow reproductions are in docs/evidence/code-review-20261031/; native Oracle/JVM and Windows qualification remain separate.
- Resolve password-file parents against canonical allowed roots and reject directory-symlink escapes while retaining no-follow/inode checks on the file (A21).
- Bind Composer predicate identifiers to verified columns/SQL words and reject unresolved bare parameterless routines in both row predicates and write authorization (CMP013, CMP014, CMP037).
- Make full APEXlang restore use the reviewed backup alias consistently during import and post-import verification; cover a backup alias different from the current configured alias (A13).
- Upgrade the vulnerable locked dependencies, starting with direct Zod 4.6.2 and the relevant MCP SDK fixes. The authorized runtime and complete dependency audits report the same nine affected packages, with no additional packages from dev dependencies; assess reachability individually, preserving the distinction between current stdio execution and HTTP/OAuth advisories. Verify oversized-input handling and the existing CLI/MCP/packaging contracts. No dependency or runtime fix was applied by this review.

 Connected and host qualification

- Broaden Decisions labels beyond the four live-checked scenarios and qualify cold-process distributions, backend-cache conditions and native-host authoring separately. The 2026-10-29 run has 20 successful warm measurements per scenario, 80/80 declared group/isolation checks, and three HTTP fallbacks among 92 attempts. Preserve failures in reporting and compare only equal-quality outcomes; investigate HTTP status/retry guidance when failures recur. Review the initial 0.5 threshold against broader labels rather than treating these fixed cases as general accuracy.
- Extend A261-069 beyond the single 26.1 sales-dashboard pilot using adaptive native-host contract reads/search and additional page types. Three runs per flag reached the same offline compiler/46-check threshold: 344.31 s disabled versus 178.05 s enabled, including one timeout fallback. Retain the fixed two-template retrieval and exploratory completion-policy limits; all failed attempts are counted. Generator usage is known, but the timed-out Decisions request has no usage, so exact enabled-arm token savings remain unavailable. Review local Ukrainian dashboard ranking, which selected less relevant templates, without rewriting the measured baseline. Keep 26.2 and connected/browser qualification separate.

- The APEX 26.1.5 read-only P0/P1 comparison passed 20 samples plus one excluded warm-up for metadata and planning. Metadata median improved from 9.62 to 5.42 seconds; plan from 6.86 to 3.13 seconds. The common full working-copy apply uses four connected sessions in fake-runner tests. Its estimated saved session time is 12.45 seconds; actual apply speed remains unmeasured on Oracle. A connected import benchmark needs a separately authorized target/plan and recovery scope. Preserve fresh identity/drift/post-import observations and discard-after-connected-batch policy; the same-session guard remains deferred until transport error-stop behavior is proven.
- Reuse the [APEX 26.1 server test catalog](../tests/plugin-server/README.md) (69 baseline and quality/performance cases), nine host-browser shell/session cases, current-build MCP runner and host time/token checkpoints. The authorized 26.1.5 title-import/reset and exact 21-file final audit passed; retain their private evidence and baseline. Extend metadata object/signature fixtures, separately planned backup restore, real fault recovery, Composer runtime and fresh host/platform scenarios with their required targets and authorization. Use the separate 20-repetition read-only benchmark for cold/warm latency; model-driven workflow and historical regression comparisons require their own controlled baseline. The local Codex plugin was refreshed to 2.1.0 on 2026-10-21; open a fresh native session to verify the hyphenated-workspace fix currently confirmed only in the current build.

title: Publishing policy
text:
Publishing policy

[apexrest-dev/apexrest](https://github.com/apexrest-dev/apexrest) is the canonical source repository. Git commits, registry packages, signed release artifacts and a deployed website are separate distribution outcomes.

Source version 2.5.0 does not inherit the retained 2.2.0 npm local-evidence exception. Any requested publication requires current applicable evidence and authorization. The retained 2.2.0 setting requires both publisher opt-ins, enabled and npmEnabled. Its explicit npmReadiness exception is bound to version 2.2.0: the three current local reports (composer-local.json, local-checks.json, oracle-local.json) block npm when missing, failed or stale. The six external Composer runtime/new-chat, native macOS/Linux/Windows and connected Oracle reports are advisory for this npm version. Their actual missing, blocked and stale states remain visible; they still block full qualification. A different package version does not inherit this exception.

Run npm run check-release-readiness -- --npm for npm eligibility. The default npm run check-release-readiness continues to require all nine reports for full qualification and signed release packaging. Both commands report npmReady, stableReady, qualification status and each report's required scope. npm eligibility does not establish full Oracle/native qualification.

These settings run no publication command. Keep local checks, successful CI on the final source, package inventory/integrity, verified registry ownership and fresh registry installation with CLI/MCP/reference checks. The release and trusted Oracle/native integration workflows remain disabled in GitHub, and their jobs use if: ${{ false }}. CI runs automatically only on pushes to main. GitHub release/tag and integration execution require separate authorization.

Full qualification and signed releases require current evidence bound to the exact immutable source, archive integrity, protected target/approval settings and an externally managed signing key where required. Missing, blocked or stale required evidence fails its applicable gate. Database deployment safeguards, production refusal and unknown-outcome recovery are unchanged.

 Documentation on GitHub Pages

The documentation website is [apexrest-dev.github.io/apexrest](https://apexrest-dev.github.io/apexrest/). The repository's Pages configuration serves the /docs directory on main, with no custom domain. Its entry point is docs/index.html, and all page, asset and search routes use the /apexrest/ base path.

The existing Markdown renderer builds the website locally:

sh
npm ci --ignore-scripts
npm run site:build
npm run site:check
npm run docs:check
npm run site:preview


Open the preview at http://127.0.0.1:4173/apexrest/. It serves the same tracked HTML and assets that Pages will serve. Search uses a local JSON index; the website needs no server-side runtime, external fonts or third-party search service. The optional APEXREST_SITE_PORT changes the preview port.

Edit the Markdown sources and site/ theme/configuration, then rebuild. Commit the generated HTML, CSS, JavaScript, search index, .nojekyll and docs/site-manifest.json together with their sources. The manifest lists files owned by the generator; the build preserves authored Markdown, catalog/reference data, diagrams and examples. site:check detects stale tracked output. The .nojekyll file lets Pages serve the prepared static files directly, following [GitHub's static-site instructions](https://docs.github.com/en/pages/getting-started-with-github-pages/creating-a-github-pages-site). Existing flat .html guide URLs remain readable with their original anchors.

site-dist/ remains an ignored staging directory for release packaging. For an alternate local preview only, use APEXREST_SITE_BASE_PATH=/ node scripts/build-site.mjs --preview; this does not update the branch-hosted docs/ output. scripts/publish-site.sh supports an explicitly authorized mounted copy, with --dry-run before --apply; it is not needed for GitHub Pages.

Building or previewing changes publishes nothing. An authorized push to main updates the branch-hosted Pages site independently of the disabled product-release publisher. Confirm the live Pages build and browser result separately after that push. No additional Pages workflow is required for this configured branch source.

See [release notes](release-notes.md), [testing](testing.md) and [next actions](next-actions.md).

title: Current release notes
text:
Current release notes

 Source bundle 2.5.0

The repository bundle supports Codex and Claude Code with six skills and twelve MCP tools. It includes APEX 26.1 full imports and [APEX 26.2 partial imports](apex-26.2.md), pinned release profiles, advisory scanner/upgrade diagnostics and read-only capability checks. Use the repository installation for this source version; registry packages are a separate distribution path.

Application verification uses the host in-app browser. The bundle has no automated application test runners, saved browser-authentication state or browser installation. Client dependencies are Node.js, Java and SQLcl. Compiler, target, backup, drift and readback protections remain in the deployment path. Full imports can end the interactive session; sign in again in the host browser when needed.

 Changes in 2.5.0

- Add [cross-vendor peer review](configuration.mdcross-vendor-peer-review): apexrest_peer_review / apexrest peer review asks the other agent CLI (Codex from Claude Code, Claude Code from Codex) for a read-only review of a saved ship plan under the user's own sign-in. The verdict is bound to the plan digest; optional peerReview.mode advisory reports it at apply and required blocks apply without an approving review. Without a plan it reviews the local sources instead, for local-only work with no Oracle target; that source-bound verdict is advisory and never unlocks required apply. The MCP catalog grows to twelve tools; its byte budget rises to 14,700 bytes.
- The [local preview](local-preview.md) follows Oracle semantics more closely: NULL for empty items, real division and Oracle number text, date arithmetic, ANSI date literals and DEFAULT sysdate in seed scripts, JSON functions, nested LISTAGG, POSIX regular expressions and ISO dates in form DML.
- Page submits, server-side code and grid saves are transactional; an unhandled process error is shown to the user and rolls back the page's DML. Interactive grid row validations mark failing cells, validation messages substitute labels, forms detect lost updates and region refreshes submit their page items.
- APEX 26.2 syntax for show-all pagination, card actions, &COLUMN. substitution, list views and calendar views is rendered; template components apply format masks; chart ticks no longer show spurious decimals.
- Items and layout match APEX more closely (switches, floating labels, grid offsets, native date pickers, static button IDs, region display selector, maps). The preview warns about unknown APEXlang property names and values.
- The README now presents APEXREST as a Codex and Claude Code plugin with three feature videos, including a new tour of a 22-page showcase application running in the preview.
- Align package, workspace and Codex/Claude Code source versions to 2.5.0. Registry distribution and full native/Oracle qualification remain separate outcomes.

 Changes in 2.4.0

- Add the [local preview](local-preview.md): apexrest preview and apexrest_preview run APEXlang sources on Node.js without an Oracle database for fast design iteration. Pages render with Universal Theme 26.2 templates and JavaScript extracted once from the official distribution.
- Cover most APEX UI/UX locally: interactive reports and editable interactive grids saved to SQLite, faceted search and smart filters on Oracle's own widget, cards and list views, Universal Theme template components with full template directives, tabs, carousel, region display selector and inline dialogs, SVG charts, FullCalendar calendars, offline maps, genuine page item widgets, a PL/SQL subset interpreter wired into processes, validations, conditions, computations and dynamic actions, and a theme-style picker. Each area is a registered feature module.
- Extend the preview with interactive report Actions-menu views, saved reports and .xlsx downloads, more interactive grid editors, tree and search regions, wizard and legacy features, file uploads, BLOBs and data loading, apex_collection, APEX dictionary views generated from the source, a local e-mail outbox, REST data from JSON fixtures, and a developer toolbar with session state, debug log, "view as" roles and tablet/phone viewports.
- Serve the APEX submit protocol, inline validation messages, modal dialogs, reports, forms, cards, lists and simple dynamic actions against SQLite, with Oracle SQL shims, .apex-local/.sql seeding and on-demand sample tables. PL/SQL beyond plain DML, APEX_ views, authentication and several region types are reported as unsupported.
- The MCP catalog grows to eleven tools; its byte budget rises to 13,600 bytes. The preview is a design aid and does not replace compiler validation, an authorized import or browser verification on DEV/QA/TEST.
- Optional [OpenAI Decisions selection](component-catalog.mdoptional-openai-decisions-selection) from 2.3.0 is unchanged.
- Align package, workspace and Codex/Claude Code source versions to 2.4.0. Registry distribution and full native/Oracle qualification remain separate outcomes.

 Upgrade a working copy

Working copies bind their runtime/toolchain version. Reconcile local edits and unresolved outcomes, then explicitly refresh a clean checkpoint with apexrest apex sync --env dev --action refresh --json and create new plans. Never edit stored runtime versions or clear unknown ownership to bypass these checks.

 Distribution and verification

Repository release and Oracle integration workflows remain disabled. The retained publisher local-evidence exception is bound to 2.2.0 and does not apply to 2.5.0. Publication requires its applicable authorization and current source-bound gates. CI runs on pushes to main only. Local packaging does not publish npm, create a Git tag or deploy a website.

See [implementation status](implementation-status.md), [acceptance](acceptance.json), [open checks](next-actions.md) and [publishing](publishing.md). Fixtures and offline compilation do not establish connected Oracle, authenticated application browsing or native model-host execution.
